facts.statement: Adjust the driving seat and mirrors before starting to drive.
The seating position should allow a clear view and full use of the pedals and steering wheel.
Leave room for the airbag to deploy when selecting the driving position.
Position the seat so the foot can pivot between brake and accelerator while the heel stays on the floor.
If the vehicle has an adjustable steering wheel or column, that adjustment may also be used when setting the driving position.
The top of the steering wheel should stay at or below shoulder height and below the chin.
The seat-adjustment paragraph calls for 10 inches between the body and the lower steering wheel.
Do not move the seat forward so far that steering becomes difficult.
Do not recline so far that reaching the wheel or using the mirrors becomes ineffective.
Use a seat cushion or pedal extensions if needed to improve the driving view.
Head restraints help protect against whiplash in a rear impact.
Whiplash involves neck pain after crash forces move the neck beyond its normal range.
Set the head restraint against the back of the head at no lower than ear level.
Aim the inside rearview mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind.
Set a day-and-night mirror for the time of day in which you are driving.
For traditional mirror adjustment, first set the seat and sit upright.
The traditional left mirror setting shows the vehicle's left edge.
The traditional right mirror setting shows the vehicle's right edge.
For trucks, vans and SUVs, traditional mirror settings may suit towing or backing in a confined area.
Passenger-car side mirrors are not designed to serve as the method for backing the car.
Enhanced mirror adjustment uses a leaned head position while setting the side mirrors.
With the enhanced setting, the vehicle's sides are not visible during an ordinary glance at the outside mirrors.
The handbook attributes an extra 12 to 16 degrees of viewing area on each side to enhanced mirror adjustment.
Enhanced mirror adjustment may not suit every vehicle, so traditional settings may be appropriate.
Fasten your safety belt before moving the vehicle.
Check that passengers use safety belts or suitable child restraints before departure.
Lock the vehicle doors before driving.
Use the childproof door locks when children ride in the vehicle.
Safety belts lower the chance of injury or death in a crash.
Safety belts permit ordinary movement but lock during a crash.
A safety belt helps prevent a rider from being ejected or striking the vehicle interior.
A safety belt helps a driver remain behind the wheel to retain steering control.
Kansas prohibits driving without a safety belt under the law described in this section.
Kansas prohibits riding in a front seat without a safety belt under the law described in this section.
Wear a safety belt on every trip, including short journeys and lower-speed roads.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Adjust the steering wheel or column if the vehicle provides that adjustment.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: If the vehicle has an adjustable steering wheel or column, that adjustment may also be used when setting the driving position.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The imperative changes an available adjustment into an instruction to make it whenever equipped.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: A seat cushion or pedal extensions may help provide a suitable view and reach when needed.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Use a seat cushion or pedal extensions if needed to improve the driving view.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Reach adds a purpose not expressly stated in this aid sentence; the source names improved view.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Traditional mirror settings may suit towing or maneuvering larger passenger vehicles in confined spaces.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: For trucks, vans and SUVs, traditional mirror settings may suit towing or backing in a confined area.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Maneuvering broadens backing, and larger passenger vehicles replaces named vehicle categories.
